end.summary:
Practised the relation 1 + 3 + 5 + … + (2n−1) = n².
Saanvi identified 1 through 19 as ten consecutive odd numbers and gave 100.
They repeatedly treated any collection of odd numbers as having a square sum.
The distinction that the sequence must start at 1 and include consecutive odd numbers was not corrected by the end.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised how adding consecutive odd numbers starting at 1 produces square numbers. Saanvi used the ten-odd-numbers pattern to give 100 and connected 25 with 5 × 5. They mixed up the rule by applying it to 3 + 5 + 7 + 9; this was still not corrected at the end. At home, ask them to check whether a list starts at 1 and contains every odd number before deciding that its sum is a square.
